Driverless cars would reduce the amount of drivers getting in accidents\")", "quality": "Balanced consideration of opposing views", "description": "The essay demonstrates nuanced thinking by conceding genuine benefits of driverless cars while still defending its position, rather than presenting a one-sided view."}, {"evidence": "Essay A develops distinct argumentative points across paragraphs (cost, driver carelessness, machine fallibility/liability) each with reasoning and development", "quality": "Organized multi-point argument structure", "description": "The essay builds a coherent case through several developed, distinct reasons that each receive their own paragraph of elaboration."}, {"evidence": "Essay A reasons through implications such as \"Wouldn't this mean that drivers who are showing less interest in the car itself would be at risk of crashing if the driver does not take control of it in time?\"", "quality": "Analytical reasoning", "description": "The essay pushes beyond restating the article to draw its own inferences about the consequences of semi-autonomous driving, showing deeper critical thinking."}, {"evidence": "Essay A maintains a clear thesis (\"the positives to driverless cars do not outweight those of the negatives\") and returns to it in the conclusion", "quality": "Coherent argumentative focus", "description": "The essay states its position clearly at the outset and sustains that position consistently through to a conclusion that ties back to the thesis."}, {"evidence": "Essay A uses more precise and varied vocabulary and sentence structures, such as \"mass produce,\" \"faulty,\" \"longrun,\" and complex conditional reasoning", "quality": "More sophisticated language control", "description": "The essay demonstrates greater command of academic vocabulary and complex sentence construction than Essay B's simpler, more repetitive phrasing."}]}
